statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1 such that nums[i] != nums[i+1]. Equivalently, r is the minimum number of operations needed to make all elements of nums equal, where one operation chooses a prefix length p with 1 <= p <= len(nums) and an integer k and adds k to every element in positions 0 through p-1.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail, overflow, go out of bounds, or panic).
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= len(nums)-1.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every i and j with 0 <= i < len(nums) and 0 <= j < len(nums), nums[i] = nums[j].
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(nums)-1 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, nums[i] != nums[i+1].
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every integer c and every slice nums2 with len(nums2) = len(nums) and nums2[i] = nums[i] + c for all 0 <= i < len(nums), and with -1000000000 <= nums2[i] <= 1000000000 for all such i, if min_operations(nums) returns r and min_operations(nums2) returns r2, then r = r2.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let rev be the slice of length len(nums) defined by rev[i] = nums[len(nums)-1-i] for every 0 <= i < len(nums). If min_operations(nums) returns r and min_operations(rev) returns rrev, then r = rrev.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let comp be the slice obtained from nums by replacing each maximal contiguous block of equal elements by one occurrence of that common value; formally, if the maximal constant blocks of nums are B_0, ..., B_{m-1} in order, then len(comp) = m and comp[j] is the common value on B_j. If min_operations(nums) returns r and min_operations(comp) returns rc, then r = rc.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every integer m with 1 <= m and len(nums)*m <= 100000, let nums2 be the slice of length len(nums)*m defined by nums2[t*m + q] = nums[t] for every t with 0 <= t < len(nums) and every q with 0 <= q < m. If min_operations(nums) returns r and min_operations(nums2) returns r2, then r = r2.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = D - 1, where D is the number of distinct values occurring in nums, that is, the cardinality of the set {nums[i] : 0 <= i < len(nums)}.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000, and nums is non-decreasing: for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)-1, nums[i] <= nums[i+1].

statement: Let r be the value returned by the function. There exists a sequence of exactly r operations that transforms nums into an array all of whose elements are equal, where each operation chooses an integer p with 1 <= p <= len(nums) and an integer k and adds k to each of the elements at positions 0 through p-1.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 100000 inclusive, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
